catholic-encyclopedia-1913-brooklyn: A 1913 entry on Brooklyn — the New York diocese of the boroughs. Thomas Meehan tells its immigrant story. The parishes rose with the tenements. The bridge joins it to Manhattan. A see of the great city's east. Its brownstones line the old streets.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-josse-raveste: This 1913 reference piece on Ravesteyn — the Louvain theologian. Jacques Forget honors his famous works. His pen served the Belgian schools. The council prized its learned son. The sixteenth century knew his name. His 1570 death is famed. His 1570 works are famed.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-nicolas-gedoy: This biographical entry profiles Nicolas Gédoyn, a French translator of the classics in the 1700s, tracing his career, his versions of Quintilian and others, and his scholarship as the 1913 editors recorded it. A compact life from the encyclopedia's scholarly gallery, preserved among its records of Florentine humanists.
jefferson-and-his-colleagues-a-chronicle: Allen Johnson's chronicle of Jefferson and his colleagues: the Virginia dynasty. The early republic's masters, vividly drawn. Founding fathers, well told. the-adventures-of-kathlyn: Harold MacGrath, author of The Man on the Box, wrote The Adventures of Kathlyn, printed at Indianapolis by the Bobbs-Merrill Company with rights held in 1914 and a warm note to W. N. Selig. Chapters listed run from The Golden Girl and The Unwelcome Throne through The Court of the Lion, Quicksands, The Slave Mart, The White Elephant, and The Seven Leopards.
the-geste-of-duke-jocelyn:
Jeffery Farnol wrote The Geste of Duke Jocelyn as a romance made for his daughter Gillian, printed in 1920 with color pictures by Eric Pape. A verse letter to Gillian opens the book.

Farnol tells his girl he will fill the book with romance from cover to cover, as the old tale-tellers wrote: in prose, blank verse, and rhyme. Gillian, grown too old for fairy tales, had sighed that novels lack love enough. Her father answers with a duke's geste of sighing lovers, quests, and high deeds, framed as a gift that she may one day read to children of her own.
the-recollections-of-geoffrey-hamlyn: Henry Kingsley's Geoffrey Hamlyn recalls the pioneer days of Australia. The warm and generous novel follows settlers through bush hardship and joy. Old England and young Australia intertwine throughout. A beloved classic of colonial life.
